chunks: Al-Tatarri from Ja'far ibn Sam'ah from 'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) who said:
I asked him about the qibla (direction of prayer). He said, 'Place the kid goat on your neck and pray.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And when the sky is completely covered with clouds and the person cannot find a sign of it via the sun and stars, let him pray towards the four directions. And if he is unable to do so due to one of the preventing causes from praying four times, let him pray towards whichever direction he wishes, and that is sufficient in case of necessity.'

key_terms.الْجَدْي: Kid goat (used here as a marker or weight)

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim determine the qibla for prayer when the sky is completely cloudy and celestial navigation is impossible?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *ikhtiyar* (choice) in qibla direction during overcast conditions, prescribing prayer towards the four cardinal points to ensure validity. The accompanying commentary by Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the hierarchy of obligation: while praying four times is ideal, praying once towards any direction is sufficient (*mujiz*) under genuine necessity (*idtirar*), reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on ease in ritual purity and direction.
